request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's own figures when a person on the sheet has the user's name
(by name or alias, as names are compared): that person's due-total and overdue-total; nothing when
there is no such person.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user's own due-total and overdue-total, and all 4 acceptance tests pass on `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:** it looks for the person on the sheet whose name or one of whose aliases matches the user's name. As elsewhere in the app, case and surrounding spaces are ignored, so "VIC" matches user "vic". If someone matches, it shows their due-total (`my-due-total`) and overdue-total (`my-overdue-total`), the same figures as their row in the people list. If nobody matches, both are blank.

**What changed:** only the front end, in two files. No server, stored data or audit changes were needed.
- `src/main/frontend/features/claims/useSheetTotals.ts` now also returns each person's own due-total and overdue-total. These come from the same per-person figures the sheet totals are built from, so the numbers always agree.
- `src/main/frontend/features/header/header.slot.tsx` finds the matching person and shows their two figures.
